title: Migration Validation, Idempotency and Deployment Checks
learningObjectives: Explain how migration history prevents reapplying a completed version.
Define idempotency and distinguish it from blindly rerunning DDL.
Use SQLite metadata queries to validate table columns.
Verify applied migration versions and key data invariants.
Create a deployment checklist with schema, data and application checks.

understand.concept: A reliable migration process validates both schema and data after applying changes. Idempotency means a deployment process can safely detect an already-applied migration and avoid applying the same non-repeatable change again.
understand.whyItMatters: Validation and migration history reduce deployment surprises and make database releases repeatable across environments.
understand.analogy: A migration is like a numbered building renovation plan: each change has a recorded step, a verification and a recovery plan.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model transactional DDL, locking, data backfills, version checks or application compatibility.

explain.narrative:
## Idempotency
A migration runner should check the migration history before applying a version. Do not blindly rerun ALTER TABLE statements that would add the same column twice. Use migration version records and explicit preconditions.

## Validation checks
Verify required tables, columns, indexes, constraints, row counts and data invariants. Use PRAGMA table_info and sqlite_schema in SQLite. Run foreign_key_check when foreign keys are involved.

## Deployment checklist
Test from a representative starting schema, apply the migration, verify the target schema and data, test application compatibility, and record the exact migration version and deployment evidence.

### Idempotency
A migration is idempotent only when repeating it produces the same intended state without duplicate or destructive side effects. IF NOT EXISTS and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING help with selected SQLite statements, but they do not make a multi-step migration automatically idempotent. Check the migration version before applying a step and validate the schema afterwards.

### Deployment checklist
Validate migration ordering, backups, permissions, schema state, data invariants, foreign keys, application compatibility and rollback or forward-fix plans. Run checks against a staging copy before production deployment.

examples.title: Create a table and migration history
examples.code: CREATE TABLE mig18_inventory (item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, item_name TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE mig18_history (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, description TEXT NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: Creates the inventory table and migration ledger. IF NOT EXISTS allows safe re-execution of this particular creation step, but a migration runner should still verify the resulting column definitions and constraints.

examples.title: Record a baseline version idempotently
examples.code: INSERT INTO mig18_history VALUES (1, 'Create inventory') ON CONFLICT(version) DO NOTHING;
examples.explanation: Records baseline version 1 with ON CONFLICT(version) DO NOTHING. This SQLite-specific UPSERT form makes repeated execution idempotent for the version key; it does not make every possible migration statement safe to repeat.

examples.title: Inspect the required table columns
examples.code: SELECT name, type FROM pragma_table_info('mig18_inventory') ORDER BY cid;
examples.explanation: Uses SQLite's table-valued pragma_table_info function to inspect column names and declared types. This is an engine-specific inspection interface; other DBMS products expose their own catalog views or metadata commands.

examples.title: Verify the migration version
examples.code: SELECT version, description FROM mig18_history ORDER BY version;
examples.explanation: Reads the migration ledger to verify that version 1 is recorded. A deployment check should also compare the ledger with the actual schema and expected migration sequence.

examples.title: Check that no foreign-key violations exist
examples.code: SELECT COUNT(*) AS foreign_key_violations FROM pragma_foreign_key_check;
examples.explanation: Runs SQLite's foreign_key_check pragma and counts violations. A zero count indicates no detected foreign-key violations in the checked database; it does not replace checks for other constraints, business rules or data quality.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and verify the table structure, migration version and foreign-key check result.
practise.independentTask: Write a migration validation checklist for a customer-order database. Include table/column checks, constraints, row counts, foreign-key checks and migration history.
hints: Check the migration history before applying a version.
Do not assume ALTER TABLE can be rerun safely.
Use PRAGMA table_info to inspect SQLite columns.
Use PRAGMA foreign_key_check to inspect referential integrity.
Verify data invariants as well as schema structure.

questions.prompt: What does idempotency mean in migration deployment?
options: The process can detect and avoid reapplying a completed migration
All tables have the same primary key
questions.answer: The process can detect and avoid reapplying a completed migration
questions.explanation: A migration runner uses version history and preconditions to avoid duplicate application.

questions.prompt: Why should ALTER TABLE not be blindly rerun?
options: The same column or constraint may already exist
questions.answer: The same column or constraint may already exist
questions.explanation: Repeating a non-idempotent DDL statement can fail or change the schema unexpectedly.

questions.prompt: Which SQLite pragma inspects table columns?
questions.explanation: table_info reports column metadata for a table.

questions.prompt: Which SQLite pragma checks foreign-key violations?
questions.explanation: foreign_key_check reports rows that violate foreign-key constraints.

questions.prompt: What should a deployment validation include?
options: Schema, data, constraints, migration history and application compatibility
Only whether the migration script file exists
questions.answer: Schema, data, constraints, migration history and application compatibility
questions.explanation: A reliable deployment validates both database state and application behaviour.
